{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1vmga_ and d1y6xa1 are in the same fold and superfamily, but not the same family. d1vmga_ is 1vmg chain A in family a.204.1.2, MazG-like, under superfamily a.204.1, all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases. d1y6xa1 is 1y6x A:7-93 in family a.204.1.4, HisE-like (PRA-PH), under that same all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatase superfamily. The SCOPe-supported relationship is therefore remote homology / probable common ancestry at the superfamily level, stronger than a fold-only resemblance but weaker than a same-family assignment. It is safe to describe the pair as members of the all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatase superfamily; it would go beyond SCOPe to transfer the specific HisE PRA-PH activity, a histidine-biosynthesis role, exact substrate specificity, or detailed active-site chemistry from d1y6xa1 to the MazG-like d1vmga_, or to relabel d1y6xa1 as MazG-like.
